races.name: hamilton-park.co.uk Amateur Jockeys' Handicap

runners_data.name: Zu Run
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse dropping to 6f for first time since December but arrives off good Brighton second form over 7f
runners_data.comment: C&D winner last May but only pieces of form since; cheekpieces return off career-low mark
runners_data.spotlight: Three 7f wins; this is his first 6f run since December 2024 but he arrives after a good second at Brighton (good to firm) and holds each-way claims.

runners_data.name: Mister Sky Blue
runners_data.note: Course and distance winner with solid recent form, proven at this track and trip
runners_data.comment: Kept on well for second here 19 days ago after a break; thereabouts
runners_data.spotlight: C&D win last May (good to firm) remains his only win from 20 starts; he has run two solid races in defeat this year, however, and would seem highly likely to run his race once more.

runners_data.name: Endowed
runners_data.note: Dual 6f handicap winner returning after 252-day break, distance specialist but fitness concern
runners_data.spotlight: Won two 6f handicaps at Chepstow last June and went close in his hat-trick bid in July (7f); two lesser efforts followed and he returns to action after 252 days on the sidelines.

runners_data.name: No Nay Nevermind
runners_data.note: Only front runner in field, winless in 19 starts but can dictate uncontested fractions
runners_data.comment: Twice runner-up off a higher mark at Newcastle late last year, but now 0-18
runners_data.spotlight: 0-19; runner-up twice in 7f AW handicaps in late 2025 but this year's efforts leave her with a point to prove.

runners_data.name: Penny Mountain
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won 6f AW handicap on New Year's Day, dropping back from longer trips
runners_data.comment: Fifth at Musselburgh latest and that form has taken a few knocks since; 1m questionable.
runners_data.spotlight: 6f AW win on New Year's Day; several good runs in defeat have followed and dropping back to 6f could prove beneficial.

runners_data.name: Shoptilyoudrop
runners_data.note: Exposed maiden over 21 starts returning after 124-day break, hard to recommend
runners_data.comment: Little to shout about for some time and now 0-20; best to look elsewhere
runners_data.spotlight: Exposed 21-race maiden; ran one of her better races when fourth at Wolverhampton in February when last seen but still easy enough to swerve.

runners_data.name: Doon The Glen
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with two 6f seconds this year, visor back on and quick recent return
runners_data.comment: Only 1-32 and vast majority of his form is at sprint distances; likely to get outstayed
runners_data.spotlight: Just one win from 33 starts but he has twice finished second this year (both 6f, AW and good to firm); return to sprinting can help, as should the return of a visor, and he helps form a strong hand for Jim Goldie.

runners_data.name: Summerstorms Dream
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with slow start issues, cheekpieces added for first time
runners_data.comment: Doing best work late when 3rd over C&D (12-1) fortnight ago; one of three for Jim Goldie.
runners_data.spotlight: Slow starts have been a recurring theme since she moved into handicaps but she has hinted that her mark is in range; cheekpieces added and Eireann Cagney is booked, so there can be encouragement for an improved showing tonight.

runners_data.name: Pebble Dash
runners_data.note: Winless maiden whose recent turf form has been disappointing compared to AW efforts
runners_data.comment: 0-14 and hard to enthuse over after latest 10l defeat here when behind two of these
runners_data.spotlight: 0-15 but the odd promising effort, including a close second at Newcastle in March (7f); neither of his turf runs this summer suggest he is the answer today.

races.paceDynamic: No Nay Nevermind is the only confirmed front runner and will likely dictate terms from the start in this 9-runner field. With eight hold-up horses including Zu Run, Mister Sky Blue, Endowed, and Penny Mountain tracking behind, she can set a comfortable rhythm without early pressure. The lack of pace competition means No Nay Nevermind can control fractions and kick clear when ready. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can sit close to the pace and hold-up horses with a sharp turn of foot who can close from mid-division.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If No Nay Nevermind gets an easy lead and dictates soft fractions
scenarios.body: She can control the race throughout and prove hard to peg back despite her poor recent form, while any hold-up horse getting first run from mid-division can also capitalize. The lack of early pace pressure allows both the leader to last home and closers to time their run perfectly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closer Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely slow and the field bunches up turning for home
scenarios.body: Hold-up horses with the best finishing kicks will have optimal conditions to unleash late runs from the back. Zu Run's Brighton second form and Penny Mountain's recent consistency make them prime beneficiaries of a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Race Injection
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent/hold-up horses moves early to pressure No Nay Nevermind from the 3f pole
scenarios.body: This creates a more honest pace that suits horses who can track the leaders and sustain their effort. Mister Sky Blue's course form and Endowed's 6f specialization could prove decisive in a more truly-run race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If No Nay Nevermind sets crawling fractions and the field closes up into a cavalry charge
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure sprint from the 2f pole where tactical position and finishing speed matter most. This chaos scenario could see any horse with residual ability get up in a blanket finish.

watchPoints.text: No Nay Nevermind gets a soft lead and dictates crawling fractions that suit her stamina over speed
Zu Run's fitness after 12 days since Brighton run and whether 6f trip is sharp enough for his style
Endowed's fitness after 252-day layoff when he showed best form in regular competition
Summerstorms Dream overcomes slow start tendency that has hindered her handicap efforts
Track conditions remain genuinely good rather than riding slower which would help stamina types

races.name: Hamilton Park EBF Maiden Stakes (Hamilton Park 2YO Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Casino Star
runners_data.spotlight: March foal; £100,000 yearling; third foal from a Listed-placed 5f 2yo and 7f winner; half-brother to the 5f 2yo winner Bacor (RPR 75); top trainer is running at a 27% strike-rate with juveniles this year (20% over the past five years); high on the shortlist.

runners_data.name: Royal Heritage
runners_data.spotlight: 98,000gns yearling, 800,000euros breeze-up 2yo; seventh foal from unraced half-sister to US 1m Grade 3 winner Farhaan; closely related to 7f-1m winner Lattam (RPR 102) and a half-brother to three winners; connections had a promising juvenile winner (Alta Regina) at Lingfield recently.

runners_data.name: Sea Palace
runners_data.spotlight: February foal; 92,000gns foal, 120,000gns yearling; ninth foal from a 5f 2yo winner (including Listed; RPR 105); half-brother to five winners, including Nigel Nott (5f-6f AW; 95); trainer seeking first juvenile winner (0-9) of the season.

runners_data.name: Desert Move
runners_data.spotlight: March foal; third foal from a 6f juvenile winner (RPR 92); half-brother to the 1m2f AW winner Sharp Move; joint trainers have had three juvenile winners (11% strike-rate) this year, including Crystal Queen (same ownership) in the Hilary Needler at Beverley; market informative.

runners_data.name: My Mate Fitz
runners_data.spotlight: March foal; £75,000 vendor yearling; first foal from US Graded stakes-placed 5.5f turf 2yo winner Invincible Gal (RPR 98); already gelded; trainer has made a flying start this term with his juveniles running at over a 30% strike-rate, National Stakes winner Where Love Lives the most notable.

races.name: Robert Graham Millar Memorial Maiden Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Florida Dreams
runners_data.note: Ex-hurdler making Flat transition, 20 days since last run ideal for Sandy Thomson, needs time to find rhythm
runners_data.comment: Grade 2 bumper winner and useful over hurdles; interesting contender on this Flat debut
runners_data.spotlight: Grade 2 bumper winner in April 2023, who also won twice over hurdles (2m) for Nicky Richards; 22-1, lacked the pace to challenge when fifth of nine on Flat debut at Haydock (11.5f, soft; Yafreh about 1l ahead in fourth) three weeks ago; likely to be seen in a better light once handicapping.

runners_data.name: Glory Of The Seas
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with clear class edge on ratings, Ray Dawson excels in tactical scenarios like this
runners_data.spotlight: 550,000gns yearling; steady improvement; beaten just over 7l (fourth) by the exciting Water To Wine on seasonal reappearance at Newbury (1m3f, good), before finishing third in a hot maiden at Chester's May Festival (12.5f maiden); gelded since and this looks the perfect opportunity to strike.

runners_data.name: Yafreh
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who showed consistency in two starts, Fahey stable in good form with 10/59 strike-rate
runners_data.comment: No threat on debut but attractive pedigree suggests he could have lots more to offer
runners_data.spotlight: Brother to 7f-1m2f winner Al Mubhir (RPR 115); showed similar level of ability in his two starts, last time 6-1 when a rallying fourth at Haydock (11.5f, soft; Florida Dreams fifth) three weeks ago; slightly more required and he will soon be handicapping.

runners_data.name: Aussie Pearl
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner returning from 231-day break, Connor Beasley will use tactical advantage from the gate
runners_data.spotlight: In the mix on Leicester debut (1m maiden fillies; 7-2) last October but soundly beaten by a long odds-on favourite at Newmarket (1m2f, good) a fortnight later; off since and, even receiving the fillies' allowance, this looks a tough race in which to reappear; stamina to prove.

runners_data.name: Togeather Forever
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with minimal form, 5lb claimer riding but RPR 27 suggests outclassed here
runners_data.comment: Half-brother to four winners (three useful) but probably a longer-term prospect
runners_data.spotlight: Half-brother to four winners, including the Listed scorer Ralston Road (1m2f-1m6f); slowly into stride and always behind on debut here (1m1f novice; hooded, 40-1) a fortnight ago; this longer trip should suit but time will be his ultimate friend; highly unlikely candidate.

races.paceDynamic: Aussie Pearl will take this race along from the front with no other confirmed pace-setters in the field, setting up a sustainable gallop over this 1m3f trip. Yafreh may press from a prominent position early but the overall tempo will be modest. This controlled pace scenario heavily favours the hold-up horses who can produce late kicks, particularly Glory Of The Seas and Florida Dreams who can use their superior class. The race shape strongly benefits closers who can quicken off an uncontested lead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Classy Closer Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Glory Of The Seas gets the expected strong pace to aim at from Aussie Pearl's uncontested lead
scenarios.body: The 550,000gns son shows his superior class with Ray Dawson timing his challenge perfectly in the final furlong. His RPR advantage and steady improvement curve make him the logical beneficiary of this tactical setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Wire-to-Wire Shock
scenarios.trigger: If Aussie Pearl maintains her gallop and the closers fail to quicken sufficiently off the modest pace
scenarios.body: The 2-year-old filly capitalizes on Connor Beasley's positive tactics and her 231-day break, holding on grimly as the better-rated horses lumber into contention too late. Her Leicester third suggests she has the engine for this longer trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Poker Works
scenarios.trigger: If Yafreh can position handily behind Aussie Pearl and outkick the tearaway leader in the straight
scenarios.body: The Fahey-trained 3-year-old uses his rallying Haydock fourth as a springboard, with Shane Gray exploiting the lack of early pace. His brother Al Mubhir's 7f-1m2f winning range suggests this trip suits the family perfectly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Florida Dreams Revival
scenarios.trigger: If the ex-hurdler Florida Dreams adapts quickly to the Flat switching from bumpers and hurdles
scenarios.body: The 8-year-old's bumper and hurdles victories suggest genuine ability, with Kevin Stott's 7lb claim helping offset the 142lbs burden. His hold-up style could prove effective if the pace collapses completely in the home straight.

watchPoints.text: Glory Of The Seas settling early - if Ray Dawson gets him relaxed behind Aussie Pearl's lead, his class advantage becomes decisive
Aussie Pearl's jumping from the gates after 231 days off - rustiness could hand initiative to Yafreh in the opening exchanges
Florida Dreams adapting to Flat racing tactics - his hurdles background may leave him vulnerable to quicker ground speed
Yafreh's positioning behind the leaders - Shane Gray needs to avoid getting trapped if the pace quickens unexpectedly
The overall tempo development - if Aussie Pearl goes too slow early, it sets up a sprint finish that may not suit her stamina

races.name: Every Race Live On RacingTV Handicap

runners_data.name: Hi Lord
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who can dictate from the front, headgear removed when winning over course and distance on penultimate start
runners_data.comment: Headgear removed and doubled his tally with a narrow win over C&D a month ago
runners_data.spotlight: Headgear removed when he pounced late to beat Mount Ruapehu over C&D (good; from 3lb lower) on penultimate start; ran to an identical level on RPRs when third here last week; should give his running at a track (form figures 2613) which suits.

runners_data.name: Canaria Queen
runners_data.note: In-form prominent runner with strong recent record, carries 5lb penalty but twice successful this season
runners_data.comment: No match for stablemate Marajito over C&D (good, 9-2) last week; remains in fine fettle.
runners_data.spotlight: In-form mare; twice successful this season, including at Musselburgh (5f, Class 6, good; from 5lb lower); runner-up at Ripon on last two outings (Tees Aggregates a close third on penultimate start); has no issues with this track; merits respect.

runners_data.name: South Parade
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse struggling this season, reared at start last time and needs everything to fall right
runners_data.comment: On a dangerous mark but she doesn't look in much form
runners_data.spotlight: 8lb lower than when last successful at Thirsk (5f Class 4, good to firm; 6-4 favourite) last August; struggled this season and reared at the start when in rear throughout (behind two of these) at Ripon latest.

runners_data.name: Tees Aggregates
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who stuck on well last time, apprentice jockey takes valuable 5lb allowance
runners_data.comment: Recent efforts respectable and has a good 0-70 record; enters calculations
runners_data.spotlight: Didn't have things go smoothly but stuck on positively down the outer when closing third (Canaria Queen second) at Ripon (5f, good) a fortnight ago; two of his three wins have been at tracks with a stiff uphill finish (Beverley and Leicester) and he's handicapped to go close at the least.

runners_data.name: Pal Joey
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who won over 5f at Newcastle but has been dwelling and ineffective since, wears visor
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Newcastle (AW; from a similar mark) in January on his first attempt over 5f; less effective since, dwelling and failing to make his presence felt over C&D (tenth of 13; Class 3) latest; this race is easier and Paul Mulrennan is back aboard.

runners_data.name: Highland Bear
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse making handicap debut after 46 days off, looks work in progress based on novice form
runners_data.comment: Showed promise in all three qualifying races; makes handicap/turf debut in low-grade race
runners_data.spotlight: Signs of ability in AW novice/maidens (5f-6f) but has looked something of a work in progress; taken out of her intended handicap debut at Wetherby (5.5f, good to firm) last week because of unsuitable ground, so this projected softer surface could suit; best watched for the moment.

runners_data.name: Mount Ruapehu
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who was beaten by Hi Lord over course and distance, less competitive in recent starts
runners_data.comment: Three 6f wins on AW this year; narrow 5f turf defeat this month; shade flat latest
runners_data.spotlight: Justified favouritism at Southwell (6f) in April and pipped by Hi Lord over C&D (good) the following week; less competitive at Catterick (7f) and Carlisle (6f) on last two outings and the handicapper might have his measure.

races.paceDynamic: Hi Lord looks the most natural pace-setter from his prominent style, with Canaria Queen also likely to be handy early in this small field. The lack of confirmed front-runners means Hi Lord can dictate terms without significant early pressure, allowing him to control fractions over this sharp 5f trip. With most runners (South Parade, Tees Aggregates, Pal Joey, Highland Bear, Mount Ruapehu) preferring to come from off the pace, the race sets up as a typical sprint where the hold-up horses will need to produce their finishing kicks. This pace scenario favours the prominent runners who can avoid traffic problems and kick clear before the closers can organise their challenges.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Hi Lord and Canaria Queen break cleanly and face no early pressure
scenarios.body: The prominent pair can control the tempo and kick clear in the final furlong before the hold-up brigade can mount their challenges. Their tactical advantage over this minimum trip proves decisive against horses needing to weave through traffic.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Charge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes pedestrian allowing closers time to organise
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get the perfect setup to unleash their finishing kicks down the outside. Tees Aggregates and Mount Ruapehu benefit most from a truly-run sprint where stamina tells.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Canaria Queen Times It
scenarios.trigger: If Hi Lord goes too early and Canaria Queen can sit just behind tracking
scenarios.body: The in-form mare can use her recent race fitness to pounce late while Hi Lord pays for making the running. Her two recent seconds show she's timing her challenges perfectly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the favourites fail to fire and traffic problems emerge in running
scenarios.body: Highland Bear or South Parade could benefit from a messy race where the market leaders underperform. The pace collapses allowing a surprise winner to emerge at big odds.

watchPoints.text: Hi Lord could get an uncontested lead if no other pace angles emerge early and prove very hard to peg back
Canaria Queen carries a 5lb penalty for recent wins which could prove crucial in a tight finish
Tees Aggregates has Jack Nicholls claiming 5lb which effectively puts him level with the principals on adjusted ratings
South Parade reared at the start last time which suggests potential stalls issues that could ruin his chances
Highland Bear makes her handicap debut after a lengthy break and market support would be significant

races.name: Indigo Unified Comms Handicap

runners_data.name: No Return
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who showed promise on stable debut but needs to prove he can build on that Lingfield second
runners_data.comment: Ex-Irish gelding who's proved inconsistent for this yard having missed six months
runners_data.spotlight: A fair 6f scorer in Ireland last spring for Daniel Murphy; made a promising start for current yard with second at Lingfield (6f) in January but he's failed to build on it, a below-par fourth of seven back at Lingfield (6f) last time.

runners_data.name: Ingleby Archie
runners_data.note: Prominent type with recent Catterick third suggesting return to form, well-placed tactically for this pace scenario
runners_data.comment: Fourth on seasonal reappearance at Wetherby (5.5f; 15-8 fav); now sits 2lb lower; chance.
runners_data.spotlight: Scored twice (5f/6f) last May and took a step forward with third of seven in 6f Catterick handicap 20 days ago; not out of things from an easing mark.

runners_data.name: Pop Star
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist carrying tongue-strap from recent Carlisle success, only 2 days since last run could be concern
runners_data.comment: Scored over 5f at Carlisle ten days ago; recorded a 6f win off current mark two years ago
runners_data.spotlight: Capitalised on a reduced mark when readily defeating a next-time-out winner in ten-runner handicap at Carlisle (5f) in refitted tongue-strap 12 days ago; hampered when favourite there on Monday; seriously considered.

runners_data.name: Novak
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with solid recent Ayr second, brings strong 7f form back to 6f which may help stamina reserves
runners_data.comment: 7f runner-up at Ayr recently; return to 6f isn't an obvious plus but it's a stiff finish
runners_data.spotlight: On the go since the turn of the year but largely in good nick and he came second of nine in 7f Ayr handicap three weeks ago; must enter calculations off the same mark.

runners_data.name: Jet Warrior
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with excellent recent 6f handicap wins, low-mileage 4yo still progressing through the ranks
runners_data.comment: Has won his last two races; 10lb rise; a contender, although this softer ground a concern
runners_data.spotlight: Low-mileage 4yo who has thrived since sent handicapping, landing 6f handicaps at Ayr (good to firm) and Ripon (good) last month; another good run when third at Carlisle (6f, good to soft) last night; not taken at all lightly.

runners_data.name: Iris Dancer
runners_data.note: Sole pace-setter coming off disappointing course run 6 days ago, but course specialist who won this race last year
runners_data.comment: Her form has been mixed this season but she's a well handicapped course specialist
runners_data.spotlight: Course specialist; only sixth of nine on her first run of 2026 here over C&D six days ago but she took this prize 12 months ago, so no surprise if she bounces back; usually wears headgear but it is now removed.

runners_data.name: Impressor
runners_data.note: Hold-up veteran who bounced back to form here 6 days ago, proven course winner with strong local record
runners_data.comment: Underwhelming since promising reappearance run but he has a strong record at Hamilton
runners_data.spotlight: A three-time winner (including over C&D) here who got back on track when third of nine over C&D six days ago; goes well on soft ground, so this veteran is in the mix, especially if the rain comes.

races.paceDynamic: Iris Dancer will set an uncontested lead with No Return and Ingleby Archie settling prominently behind her, creating a modest but sustainable pace in this small field. The three hold-up horses (Pop Star, Novak, Jet Warrior, Impressor) will be bunched at the rear, setting up a classic front-versus-back tactical battle over 6f at Hamilton. With only one true pace-setter and plenty of closers, the early pace will be pedestrian before a frantic final 2f. This race shape strongly favours the prominent runners who can bridge the gap between Iris Dancer's soft lead and the backmarkers' finishing kick.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays moderate and the closers leave their runs too late
scenarios.body: No Return and Ingleby Archie can track Iris Dancer's honest pace before quickening clear in the final furlong. The hold-up horses find themselves too far back when the real acceleration begins.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Class hold-up prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely slow and the track plays fair
scenarios.body: Pop Star and Jet Warrior can unleash devastating finishing kicks from off the steady gallop. Their superior recent form and tactical speed will overhaul the leaders in the dying strides.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Iris Dancer repeats
scenarios.trigger: If she improves sharply from her recent sixth place here
scenarios.body: The course specialist can steal a march on her rivals and hold on grimly under pressure. Her intimate knowledge of this track and last year's course victory become decisive factors.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Veteran surge late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and experience tells
scenarios.body: Novak and Impressor use their racecraft to position perfectly before grinding past younger rivals. Their stamina reserves and tactical nous prove superior in a slowly-run tactical affair.

watchPoints.text: Iris Dancer could steal the race if she breaks much sharper than her recent sluggish course effort suggested
Pop Star may struggle with quick turnaround from Carlisle win just 2 days ago, watch for any signs of tiredness
No Return needs to settle better than he has recently to take full advantage of the tactical setup
The hold-up quartet could find themselves in traffic trouble if they're all still last turning for home
Jet Warrior's recent good-to-firm form may translate perfectly to today's good going conditions

races.name: Hampton By Hilton Hamilton Park Handicap

runners_data.name: Mwafaq
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with hat-trick form but needs strong pace to unleash finishing kick from rear
runners_data.comment: Chance was compromised at Southwell by a wide trip; remains of interest
runners_data.spotlight: Won reappearance, completing the hat-trick, at Thirsk (7f, good; from 4lb lower) in April; pressed the winner hard at Ayr (1m, good to firm) three weeks ago; this is a slightly longer trip; useful claimer in the saddle.

runners_data.name: The Sweet Escape
runners_data.note: Prominent racer dropping back in trip, won last start but from lower mark
runners_data.comment: C&D win last month; went close at Leicester on penultimate start; needs more in this grade
runners_data.spotlight: Took advantage of a drop back in trip and ease in grade (into a Class 6) when scrambling home at Nottingham (8.5f, good; from 3lb lower) in April; beaten by a nose off this mark at Leicester (1m) in May and consistent since; possible.

runners_data.name: Pisanello
runners_data.note: Dual course winner whose best days are behind him but dangerous off bottom weight with claimer
runners_data.comment: 9yo who is nothing like the force of old but his Hamilton fourth wasn't devoid of promise
runners_data.spotlight: Dual C&D winner; failed to score since York (1m1f, Class 4) two years ago; way down the weights now and 4l fourth to Perfidia over C&D (now 4lb lower and claimer ridden) on penultimate start, but usual tale of modest late headway continued at Carlisle last time; patience with him is wearing thin.

runners_data.name: Condotti
runners_data.note: Still maiden after eleven starts, needs to overcome poor recent form but well-handicapped
runners_data.comment: Ten-race maiden but he ran some good races last season and reappears on a career-low mark
runners_data.spotlight: Still seeking first win (0-11) and now 10lb lower than when runner-up at Ffos Las (1m, good; 2-1 favourite) last August; weakened quickly when last of nine on reappearance at Carlisle (1m1f, good) 12 days ago.

runners_data.name: Hunterian
runners_data.note: Showed improvement on turf debut, three-year-old getting weight allowance against older rivals
runners_data.comment: Unexposed; makes turf debut down in trip after four runs on AW; has a bit to prove
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten in four AW starts (at around a mile); took a slight step forward, showing speed, when third on turf debut at Redcar (7f, good to firm; 12-1) a fortnight ago; opposition suitable, but this return to 8.5f may not help; low mileage.

runners_data.name: Perfidia
runners_data.note: Course winner with strong recent form, hold-up style needs genuine pace to be effective
runners_data.comment: He's been in good form since returning to action and could be in the shake-up
runners_data.spotlight: Did enough to justify favouritism over C&D (good; from 2lb lower; Pisanello fourth) three back; held form reasonably well since, failing to get the breaks at Ripon (1m, good; fifth) last week; Jake Dickson's 7lb claim continues to be handy.

runners_data.name: Spirit Catcher
runners_data.note: Only confirmed front runner, stamina questions over this trip but controls tactics
runners_data.comment: Arrives in form, winning over 1m1f here before a good 2nd at Ripon; new trip; key player
runners_data.spotlight: Returned to winning ways at Musselburgh (1m1f, good; from 4lb lower) in April and runner-up twice since, stamina seemingly overstretched behind the thriving Alpine Sierra at Musselburgh (12.5f) latest; enters calculations back over a more suitable 8.5f.

runners_data.name: Motawaared
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner struggling since yard switch, slowly away habit is major tactical concern
runners_data.comment: Did not get seriously competitive when seventh on first two starts this season (1m4f/1m1f)
runners_data.spotlight: Placed in a novice and a maiden (both 1m) for George Boughey; low key (0-4, often slowly away) since joining Jim Goldie for 12,000gns; drops into a Class 6 for the first time, though, with cheekpieces added; no forlorn hope.

runners_data.name: South Road
runners_data.note: Limited performer whose shock win came on different ground, returning from break
runners_data.comment: 40-1 winner of a 6f handicap here last summer; there are stamina doubts over this far
runners_data.spotlight: Shock 6f winner at Ayr (good to soft; 40-1, from 5lb higher) last July; not much to enthuse about since (0-5) but she was returning from a two-month break when fifth at Ayr (1m, good to firm; Mwafaq runner-up) latest; stamina is a major risk over 8.5f.

runners_data.name: Tees George
runners_data.note: Won two starts ago but disappointed latest, needs to rediscover Beverley form
runners_data.spotlight: Fourth of 22 at Doncaster (1m, good to soft) in March and built on that when winning at Beverley (8.5f) the following month; latest Beverley effort was not so good and he has fared no better than sixth in six races from a mark of 61 and higher.

runners_data.name: Millbuie
runners_data.note: Winless in twenty-five starts, third latest but this tougher despite good handicap position
runners_data.comment: Yet to win but he comes here on the back of a solid Ayr sixth; more is still needed
runners_data.spotlight: 25-race maiden; had run of the race at Newcastle (1m2f; third, 16-1) last week but was unable to make it count; no reason to think that this return to turf can unlock the door; others are more convincing.

races.paceDynamic: Spirit Catcher will take the field along from the front with minimal pressure, as The Sweet Escape and Condotti are the only other prominent runners but both lack early pace intensity. This creates a comfortable, controlled gallop that will build gradually through the middle sections before quickening in the straight. The lack of genuine speed horses means the pace will be steady rather than strong, with Spirit Catcher able to dictate terms without harassment. This tactical setup strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can position close to the pace, as hold-up horses will face a sprint finish from an already moderate tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Spirit Catcher gets an easy lead without pressure from prominent runners
scenarios.body: Spirit Catcher controls the tempo completely and kicks clear in the straight before hold-up horses can mount their challenge. The combination of a soft lead and stamina-testing distance plays perfectly into the hands of the lone pace-setter.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pressure Applied
scenarios.trigger: If The Sweet Escape or Condotti press Spirit Catcher early and force a stronger pace
scenarios.body: The increased tempo exposes Spirit Catcher's stamina limitations over this extended trip, allowing late-running types to close strongly. Hold-up horses like Perfidia and Mwafaq benefit from the honest gallop and can unleash their finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Messy Moderate Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners fail to commit and create a stop-start rhythm
scenarios.body: The lack of consistent tempo creates a tactical muddle that favours horses with tactical speed who can quicken when gaps appear. Runners with recent form progression and tactical pace like Hunterian can exploit the disjointed race shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish Lottery
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes crawling throughout
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure sprint from the final two furlongs, turning into a lottery where any horse with a turn of foot can win regardless of position. This chaotic finish could throw up an outsider with residual ability but questionable recent form.

watchPoints.text: Spirit Catcher breaking smartly and getting uncontested lead - makes him extremely difficult to peg back
The Sweet Escape and Condotti settling kindly in prominent positions without pressing the pace too early
Motawaared's starting position and early alertness - slow starts have cost him repeatedly
How strongly Perfidia and Mwafaq are positioned turning for home given their hold-up styles
Hunterian's positioning on only second turf start - inexperience could cost him tactically
